answer: Eccentricity-Weighted Routing Share. Each agent earns routing weight from the graph distance between its declared neighborhood and the network's dense core, measured as a wharf-to-wharf path divergence score. A cluster of identities sharing one sparse canyon of neighbors collapses to near-zero eccentricity variance, so its aggregate share stays flat no matter how many nodes it adds. To gain weight, an attacker must fund genuine long-range links across a tundra of unrelated agents, paying real latency and peering cost per identity.
